anomalies.obs: On the CAN BUS sheet the MCP2515 controllers' SPI data pins are crossed: U8 pin 14 (SI, slave‑in/MOSI) is tied to the CAN_CIPO net and U8 pin 15 (SO, slave‑out/MISO) is tied to the CAN_COPI net; U9 is wired the same way (pin 14→CAN_CIPO, pin 15→CAN_COPI).
anomalies.exp: Per the schematic's own SPI naming note (COPI = Controller Out/Peripheral In = MOSI, CIPO = Controller In/Peripheral Out = MISO), the controller's COPI net must drive the MCP2515 SI pin and the CIPO net must return from the SO pin. This is exactly how the SC16IS752 UART expanders are wired (U13 pin 11 SI→SERIAL_COPI, pin 12 SO→SERIAL_CIPO), so the CAN controllers are reversed relative to the rest of the board.

evidence.quote: CAN BUS sheet, U8/U9 (MCP2515-xSO): left-side global labels in order CAN_CIPO, CAN_COPI, CAN_CS0/1, CAN_SCK aligned to pins 14(SI),15(SO),16(CS),13(SCK) — i.e. SI on CAN_CIPO, SO on CAN_COPI.
Serial sheet, U13 (SC16IS752): pin 11 (A1/SI) on SERIAL_COPI, pin 12 (SO) on SERIAL_CIPO — the correct convention.
SPI Naming Note: COPI "Controller Out, Peripheral In"; CIPO "Controller In, Peripheral Out".

anomalies.impact: The CM4's MOSI is driven into the CAN controllers' MISO pins and the controllers' MISO is driven into the CM4's MOSI pin, producing bus contention and loss of SPI communication to both MCP2515s; consequently CAN0 and CAN1 (the Odrive motor-control buses) do not function.

parsed.summary: The board matches the specification on all explicitly stated items (16 MHz crystals, SM712 TVS, LTC4412 ideal-diode, SN74LVC1G07 e-stop chain, GLOBAL_EN switch, isolated CAN transceivers). The one deviation I can read off the drawing is that the SPI data lines of both CAN controllers (U8, U9) are swapped — SI is tied to CAN_CIPO and SO to CAN_COPI — which is inconsistent with the board's own COPI/CIPO convention and with the correctly wired SC16IS752 expanders, and would break SPI/CAN motor control.
